transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-29
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Martin Lopez (CTO, Casimir AI), Sara Nguyen (ML Lead), Theo Park (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial):
Casimir AI is evaluating Redwood for a hybrid deployment: hosted for early traffic, Dedicated or Private for regulated customers and PII-sensitive flows. Main questions: multilingual model quality (Vietnamese/Korean + low-resource languages), context length requirements (32k vs 128k), tool/function calling for up-to-date user data and DB lookups, latency/cost tradeoffs, and audit/SSO/KMS needs for private deployment. Redwood recommended model families and rollout approach, and committed to benchmarks and security docs. Next: pricing, benchmarks, and a technical deep dive.

Topics: model selection, context windows, multilingual, tool calling / function calling, deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security/compliance, rollout and eval plan.

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate) ---
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for taking the time. I'm Jordan Kim, AE at Redwood. With me is Priya Shah our solutions engineer. How's everybody doing?
[00:06] Martin: Good, Jordan. Thanks. We have limited time so want to focus on model selection and the deployment story. I'm Martin, CTO at Casimir. Sara's gonna cover ML needs. Theo is here for infra questions.
[00:15] Sara: Hi all. Quick context: Casimir builds a customer-support automation product for APAC and LatAm markets, so multilingual support is critical. We expect a mix of Vietnamese, Korean, Portuguese, Spanish, and some smaller languages. We also have two main flows: real-time chat (short context but low latency) and context-rich case summaries where we need full conversation history, sometimes 50-80k tokens.
[00:37] Priya: Got it. Can you say more about the 50-80k token use case — is that a rolling window or full history?
[00:42] Sara: Mostly full history for high-value customers: pull in previous chats, KBs, attachments. We want the model to synthesize and not lose thread. We aren't wedded to storing everything in prompt, but we want high-fidelity summarization without lots of retriever hops.
[01:00] Theo: From infra: we have an existing VPC on AWS, strict egress controls, and SOC 2 in our roadmap. We are evaluating whether Redwood Hosted plus Dedicated reserved for PII flows makes sense or if we need Redwood Private in our VPC. Also curious about KMS and audit logs.
[01:17] Jordan: Makes sense. For context windows, Redwood supports models and variants with different max context — we saw you mentioned 80k — we can route long-context requests to larger-window models or to quantized 128k variants in Dedicated/Private. There's tradeoffs on latency and cost. Priya, want to take the model families?
[01:33] Priya: Sure. For multilingual and low-resource languages we've had good results with newer open families — Mistral & Mistral-derivatives, and the latest Falcon/Gemini-style open variants. Llama-family models are OK but you might see gaps in Vietnamese/Korean unless tuned. For 32k windows, a Mistral-32k style variant gives a good balance; for 100-128k you often need either model variants compiled specifically for long context or a hybrid approach: chunk + KV caching with retrieval.
[02:05] Sara: So when you say KV caching, is that like keeping token-level KV cache between requests? We were thinking of prefix caching but unclear how that interacts with streaming.
[02:14] Priya: Exactly — prefix/KV caching helps preserve the decoder state so you can avoid resending the same earlier context. It reduces token cost and latency for repeated context. Streaming still works — you stream generation tokens — but you save the forward passes for earlier tokens. Important detail: caching and cross-request reuse works best in Dedicated and Private where you control affinity and can keep sessions on GPU nodes. Hosted supports caching too but with shorter TTLs in the shared fleet.
[02:43] Martin: That affinity requirement is important. For Hosted we might do quick POC but production needs affinity guarantees. If we go Dedicated, can we set autoscale and burst? We want predictable SLOs for enterprise customers.
[02:53] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools with configurable autoscaling and burst policies. You get predictable throughput and can pin model versions. Private gives you even more control — you bring the nodes into your VPC or run on-prem, with KMS integrations and audit logs.
[03:07] Theo: And the KMS — do you support AWS KMS + HSM? We need envelope encryption and ability to rotate keys under our control.
[03:14] Priya: We support AWS KMS integration and customer-managed keys (CMKs) for Private. For Dedicated we offer managed keys with options for customer key control. HSM-backed rotation is part of our enterprise compliance add-on. We'll share the security pack with specifics.
[03:28] Sara: Back to model quality — how do you evaluate multilingual quality? We need to reproduce our in-house evals before commitment.
[03:35] Priya: We recommend a short eval harness: you can send a representative anonymized sample of chat logs (we prefer removed PII) and we run a side-by-side on a few candidate models: Mistral-32k variant, Falcon-extended, and one Llama-based tuned variant. We'll produce BLEU/ROUGE-like scores and qualitative failure cases. We'll also look at hallucination rates for KB retrieval tasks.
[03:55] Martin: Is there a risk of hallucination when doing tool-calling / function calls? We need the model to call a DB retrieval function, not hallucinate data.
[04:03] Priya: Tool calling/structured function-calling is supported. We recommend tightly constrained functions and verifying outputs with deterministic checks. For PII or sensitive queries you can route the call through a verification layer and only allow returns that match expected schemas. We also have tracing hooks in the Console to see which function calls were triggered for audit.
[04:22] Theo: On latency, what's typical for a streaming response with a 4k generation window on Mistral-32k in Dedicated?
[04:28] Priya: Median token latency is under 40ms per token on modern GPUs in Dedicated with optimized kernels; end-to-end for a ~200 token generation is usually 600-900ms. For long-context models or quantized 128k variants, latencies increase — sometimes 20-30% depending on kernel selection and batching. There's a cost tradeoff there.
[04:49] Sara: Cost tradeoffs — can you give a ballpark for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private per-token economics? We need a number to show execs.
[04:57] Jordan: We'll send a tailored pricing sheet, but roughly: Hosted is simplest and cost-effective for low-to-medium volume; Dedicated reduces unit costs at scale due to reserved capacity and autoscale efficiency; Private has a platform fee plus infra costs — best when compliance or data residency requires it. We'll illustrate with an example for 10M tokens/month in the follow-up.
[05:17] Martin: One more question on rollout: we have a small pilot for 2-3 enterprise customers starting Jan. How would we phase model updates and fallbacks?
[05:25] Priya: Redwood Console supports canary deploys, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies. You can pin certain customers to hosted production and others to dedicated backends. We'll work with you on a rollout plan: start hosted for pilot, move high-value customers to Dedicated, and for regulated ones migrate to Private after security review.
[05:41] Theo: About network: what's the egress pattern for Private — do you ever need outbound to Redwood control plane? We're air-gapped in some regions.
[05:49] Jordan: For Private deployments you can opt for an air-gapped package where the control plane interacts via your network peering or not at all; we have an option for fully isolated on-prem packages. We'll send the private deployment checklist.
[05:59] Sara: Are there examples of customers with similar multilingual heavy usage you can share benchmarks for?
[06:05] Priya: We have anonymized case studies — a telco and a fintech with multi-region usage. We'll include anonymized latency and cost numbers.
[06:12] Martin: OK great. I'm conscious of time — I'm going to hand over to Sara for three quick technical priorities so we can lock the POC scope.
[06:18] Sara: Priority 1: Achieve 95% intent detection accuracy across five languages using open models without special tuning. Priority 2: Summarization fidelity on 50-80k history with under 8% information loss. Priority 3: Deterministic DB tool-calling with structured JSON output and audit trail.
[06:35] Priya: We'll map those to a POC: (1) run multilingual evaluation on three models, (2) test long-context summarization with chunk+KV caching and a 128k candidate variant, (3) set up simple function-calling harness with validation and console tracing.
[06:52] Jordan: Next steps recap — we'll send the pricing + security pack, Priya will run benchmarks once you send sample logs, and we'll schedule a tech deep dive with Theo to discuss VPC/firewall constraints. Anything else?
[07:05] Martin: That's it. Thanks everyone.
[07:07] Jordan: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the docs and calendar invite.

(End of transcript — timestamps are approximate; speech recognition had occasional mislabels: e.g., Mistral variants transcribed as "mistle" in one spot; some proper nouns may be odd.)
